- If sentiment shows strong bullish (≥0.5) or bearish (≤-0.5) momentum in recent days, model should adjust forecast slope to match sentiment direction, especially if price has recently spiked or dipped.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., -1.0) after a peak, model often underreacts — increase forecast downward bias to reflect sentiment-driven correction.
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in early forecast windows (e.g., 30d) — apply upward bias to forecast if sentiment is bullish or if recent history shows volatility.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.25), model tends to forecast flat or slightly downward — adjust upward if recent price action shows upward momentum.
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion after strong deviations — if price deviates >15% from 30d average, apply corrective pull-back in forecast unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- Forecast horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment changes sharply within 3–5 days, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in price reaction.
